contract.words: Make $1,000 within 14 days. I have no money to start with and I will not do any of the work myself.

terms.proofCondition: First paid sale settled to the owner account

strategy.title: Zero-capital resale of white-label websites to local businesses with no website: Brain sells by email, AgencyPlatform builds, supplier paid only from settled buyer cash
strategy.why: Nothing is spent before a buyer pays: buyers pay $400 up front, Stripe pays out 7 days after the first live payment, and the $59 build plus $50 membership are bought from that settled cash. 4 sales by day 6 settle $1,600 by day 13 (net ~$1,267 after fees and supplier). The owner does no work. The close rate in a 6-day window is unknown, so a $0 test decides.

alternatives.title: White-label local SEO retainers resold at $300/month
alternatives.why: Same channel and settlement, but $300/month needs 4 retainers and a monthly service is a harder first sale in 6 days; resale price unestablished

alternatives.title: Marketplace gigs (Fiverr/Upwork)
alternatives.why: Fiverr clears revenue 14 days after completion and Upwork holds fixed-price funds 5 days after approval, so money lands after day 14; Upwork bidding also costs Connects

alternatives.title: Referral commission from a web studio
alternatives.why: Commission (6%) is paid after the referred project pays, beyond 14 days; refused by Brain on DEADLINE

steps.label: Brain builds a list of Google Maps local service businesses with no website and emails about 300 of them from a free mailbox by day 5 and 300 more on days 6-7 (600 total)
Offer: up-to-5-page mobile website for $400, paid up front by Stripe payment link, delivered within a week of payment clearing
Brain answers replies by email and sends the Stripe payment link; no owner calls
Day-6 gate: count paid orders against emails sent
AgencyPlatform builds each paid site (AI Launch, $59, 3 business days, with one month of Gold membership $50), paid only from settled Stripe payouts; Brain sends the brief and checks the result
Stripe collects $400 per sale; first payout 7 days after the first live payment

validation.proof: By day 6, at least 4 businesses have paid $400 each through the Stripe link out of the 600 emails sent, and Stripe shows the first payout dated within 7 days of the first payment
stop: The owner declines to hold a Stripe account in his name (identity and bank verification): stop before any email is sent; loss $0
Fewer than 600 no-website local businesses with a published email counted by day 2: stop; loss $0
Fewer than 4 paid by day 6: stop selling; every paid order is still built from its own settled cash, so the loss is $0
Stripe shows a first-payout wait over 7 days (the up-to-14-day industry hold): no sale can settle by day 14; stop and say so, still fulfilling any paid order
A buyer asks for a refund before delivery: refund from settled cash and do not count that sale
continue: 2 or more paid by day 6: email 300 more on days 6-7 (600 total, implying 4 sales at the proven rate) and stop taking orders after day 7 and order builds from settled cash

answers.finding: At the 2-of-300 threshold the plan reaches 2 sales by day 6 (net ~$608); 4 sales are needed (3 net ~$937), and the 300 follow-up emails on days 6-7 cannot close by the day-7 cutoff. Threshold does not carry the target.
answers.resolution: Accepted. All 600 emails go out on days 1-5 and the threshold is 4 paid of 600 by day 6, which is exactly what the target needs (net $1,266.40); there is no follow-up wave after day 6.

answers.finding: Ledger assumes 4 paid of the first 300 (1.33%), double the threshold rate.
answers.resolution: Accepted. The ledger books 4 sales (days 3-6) from 600 emails, equal to the 4-of-600 threshold.

answers.finding: MARKET_VOLUME unestablished: no count of no-website local businesses with a published email; buyerVolume research blocked.
answers.resolution: Accepted. MARKET_VOLUME is missing in the chain, in resolves and validation.decides; the reach step must count 600 by day 2 or the plan stops at $0.

answers.finding: Stripe first payout is 7 days typically but up to 14 for certain industries (s6); at 14 days no sale settles inside the window - no stop rule covers this.
answers.resolution: Accepted. A stop rule now covers it: the day-6 gate checks the payout date Stripe shows; a wait over 7 days stops the plan.

answers.finding: Owner work is forbidden, but opening a Stripe account (KYC, bank) is the owner's; unknown owner time is treated as zero. SEND_A_MESSAGE and ISSUE_AN_INVOICE are NOT_CONNECTED.
answers.resolution: Accepted in part. The owner account setup time is now an UNKNOWN quantity and the first stop rule asks it before any email: if the owner will not hold the receiving account, the plan stops at $0. Sending and payment links are connected in the reach step before any send.

answers.finding: Buyers who pay on day 2 receive nothing until the build is ordered on day 9 (+3 business days); refund/chargeback risk inside the window is unmodelled.
answers.resolution: Accepted. The offer now states the site is live within 12 days of payment, so ordering on payout (days 10-13) plus 3 business days meets the stated date; a refund request before delivery is refunded from settled cash and not counted (stop rule).

answers.finding: Price $400 sits inside the only accepted range (UENI basic site $300-$1,000) and is correctly left to the test.
answers.resolution: Agreed; OFFER_AND_PRICE stays missing and is decided by the test.

answers.finding: MARKET_VOLUME condition
answers.resolution: The card has no buyerVolume (research NO_SUPPORT) and Brain's basis applies to a single buyer; MARKET_VOLUME is treated as missing and measured.

excluded.why: Resale price unestablished; a $300 monthly retainer is a harder first sale inside 7 days and needs 4 clients; not sold in this plan
